text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi told the Women's Congress on Monday that women should be more active in national development and should receive a fair share of the benefits from that development.
-- Twenty-five people will be brought to court on May 25, charged with involvement in embezzlement and causing losses at the Nam Dinh Textile Corporation.
-- Vietnam and China held a tenth round of expert-level talks on their land border in Beijing May 6-19 in an atmosphere of friendship and frankness.
-- Vietnam will auction 50 billion ($4.28 million) worth of one-year Treasury notes on Wednesday.
-- Vietnam Women's Congress began in Hanoi on Monday with the aim of setting goals and resolutions for their movement over the next five years.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet left Vietnam on Tuesday for official visits to Poland, the Czech Republic, Italy and Hungary.
